title: Minimum Payment Terms Table — Crestline Credit Card
content:
The printed minimum payment on a Crestline Credit Card statement is built from two product figures, a payment floor in dollars and a percentage of the new balance, together with the amounts every product adds on top of it.

## Product figures

| Product | Payment floor | Percentage of the new balance |
|---|---|---|
| Crestline Auto Care Card Starter | 29 USD (29.0) | 3.5% |
| Crestline Auto Care Card | 30 USD (30.0) | 3.5% |
| Crestline Auto Care Card Preferred | 35 USD (35.0) | 3.25% |
| Crestline Auto Care Mastercard | 35 USD (35.0) | 3% |
| Crestline Auto Care Mastercard Preferred | 40 USD (40.0) | 3% |
| Crestline Auto Care World Mastercard | 40 USD (40.0) | 2.75% |

## Common terms (every product)

- **Rounding of the percentage figure:** rounded up to the whole dollar.
- **Amounts added on top of the computed minimum:** any past-due amount, the fixed monthly payment of each equal-payment plan, and a late fee posted in the cycle.
- **Payment floor:** the lower bound of the minimum, or the full new balance when that is less.
- **Percentage base:** the new balance excluding equal-payment promotional balances.

## Reading the table

The percentage of the new balance sets the minimum only when it exceeds the floor. Hypothetical figures: on a product with a 35 USD floor and a 3% percentage, a percentage base of 2,100 USD gives 63 USD, above the floor; a percentage base of 900 USD gives 27 USD, below the floor, so the floor applies.
